messages.subject: Stand Alone html Shiny Document
parts: I'm trying create a standalone html file using RStudio. I go to File then to NewFile then to R Markdown and pick Shiny. I then select Shiny Document then OK. I highlight the code and Run. After it has finished I click Run Document and it makes the Shiny documents and it opens and runs correctly, however I want to save the as a standalone html document that will run in a web browser. How do I do this?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Stand Alone html Shiny Document
parts: Unfortunately you can't do that. The whole point of shiny is that it provides interactive webpages, which means the webpage is communicating with R.  You can't simply save an HTML page and have it work, because it needs to somehow be talking with R for all the shiny stuff to work. This is why RStudio provides shinyapps.io - that's a service where you can upload your shiny apps to the web for free. You can also get your own shiny server and if it's set up properly then you can host shiny apps there, but that's more complicated. The main point is that a shiny app is *not* just a webpage, it does require a shiny server to listen (when you run an app from RStudio, the webpage that opens in your browser is connected to your rstudio session, but if you close rstudio that shiny page won't work anymore)
